batches.t: Flood Map for Planning current-zone gate
batches.c: Current EA planning flood mapping is a site-research starting point. Exact candidate coordinate/geometry and current layer response are required before any Flood Zone signal is promoted.
Flood Zones plus climate change is a future composite extent and ignores benefits of existing defences. It must not be treated as present-day inundation or parcel certainty.
FRA requirements depend on flood zone, site area, surface-water/future risk and proposal class. A coordinate alone cannot establish the final assessment obligation.
The sequential test compares reasonably available lower-risk sites and is proposal/context dependent. Flood-zone presence alone is not a pass/fail development score.
Environment Agency consultation can be required within 20 metres of a main river or flood defence. Exact distance and proposal characteristics are required.
Peak-flow and rainfall allowances depend on the correct management catchment, development vulnerability and lifetime. No national default percentage is transferred to a candidate.
Surface-water risk must use current/future mapped or modelled evidence and site-specific interpretation. Borough or catchment context is not parcel proof.
Strategic flood assessment should consider reservoirs, groundwater and other sources; reservoir mapping must not be used in isolation and groundwater may need additional datasets.
SPZ1/2/3/4 boundaries indicate groundwater pollution sensitivity around abstractions. Candidate effect requires exact zone intersection and proposal contamination pathway.
Detailed EA products can support design flood levels and residual-risk assessment. Model/product limitations and climate allowances must be retained; no score from a map screenshot alone.
Development potentially affecting a SSSI requires exact site/zone-of-influence evidence and may require Natural England consultation. Nearby protected land is not automatically a parcel constraint.

batches.t: SSSI Impact Risk Zone screening gate
batches.c: SSSI IRZs are proposal-type screening zones for consultation risk, not protected-site boundaries or automatic refusal zones. Exact IRZ and proposal category are required.
SAC effects require exact protected-site pathway and proposal relationship. European-site protection cannot be inferred from borough-level presence.
SPA effects require exact site/pathway and proposal evidence; the screening relationship is distinct from direct parcel intersection.
Ramsar sites receive habitats-site planning protection. Candidate effect requires exact site/pathway evidence and any required Habitats Regulations assessment.
Where a plan or project may significantly affect a habitats site, appropriate assessment rules can apply. Triggering depends on project effects, alone and in combination.
Protected-species decisions require species/habitat evidence and often ecological survey. A generic biodiversity layer or nearby record is not candidate-specific proof.
Ancient woodland is irreplaceable habitat. Exact woodland inventory/site relationship and direct/indirect impact assessment are required; small woods can be absent from inventories.
Ancient and veteran trees may require survey beyond inventories. Exact tree/location and construction/operational impact evidence are required before promotion.
BMV land is grades 1, 2 and 3a, but strategic ALC maps are not accurate enough for individual fields. Exact survey evidence is required for site-level conclusions.
The National Heritage List for England is the official current register for nationally protected historic buildings and sites. Candidate use requires exact asset or mapped designation binding.
A listed-building record must be matched to the actual asset and relevant setting/curtilage effects. Nearby listed buildings cannot be transferred to the candidate.
Scheduled-monument impact requires exact monument boundary/setting and proposal evidence; national category counts are context only.
Registered parks and gardens are heritage assets. Candidate impact requires exact designation/setting relationship rather than local-area presence.
Registered battlefield status is a mapped national designation. Exact boundary/setting relationship is required before any candidate constraint is promoted.
World Heritage and other national designations must be matched to the current official record and exact spatial relationship; category existence alone is not parcel evidence.
Heritage at Risk is dynamic condition/vulnerability evidence, not a new designation. Candidate effect first requires an exact underlying heritage-asset relationship.
Historic England GIS datasets are periodically refreshed and de-designations are tracked. Exact current dataset/version must be checked so removed or stale designations are not promoted.
National Highways is a statutory consultee for proposals that may affect safety, queuing, access or improvement of the SRN. Exact network relationship and proposal traffic effects are required.
Route strategies and future investment evidence describe network planning, not committed site capacity. Proposed road improvements are not treated as operational benefit without delivery evidence.
